purpose: machine-usable expert-system KB of concrete analytical and decision work-units a strategist performs to analyze competitive position and choose strategy: industry/competitive analysis, sources of competitive advantage, strategic choices, and business-model design; a subdomain node of a knowledge-searcher meta-KB for finding, evaluating, and synthesizing authoritative strategy knowledge.
assumptions: modeled as session-bounded stepwise analytical/decision work-units, not firm-specific advice
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
scope is single-business and corporate competitive strategy, not functional/marketing execution
frameworks (five forces, SWOT, PESTEL, value chain, VRIO, blue ocean, disruption) are treated as decision tools tied to a framed question
exclusions: detailed financial valuation and accounting mechanics

competency_questions.question: Given a business problem, what is the well-posed strategic question (decision, unit of analysis, horizon, criteria) it should be answered as?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STRATEGIC_QUESTION_FRAME maps the problem to a decision

competency_questions.question: How is the relevant industry/market boundary drawn, including substitutes, geography, and buyer groups?
What is the structural attractiveness of the industry and which macro and five-forces drivers set average profit potential?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIVE_FORCES_ANALYSIS and PESTEL_MACRO_SCAN rate structure with drivers

competency_questions.question: Who are the competitors, how do strategic groups map, and how will rivals likely respond to a move?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITOR_PROFILING produces profiles and response predictions

competency_questions.question: Which customer segments and jobs-to-be-done, with what willingness-to-pay, ground the value proposition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CUSTOMER_SEGMENTATION_JTBD yields need-based segments and WTP

competency_questions.question: Where in the value chain do the firm's cost and differentiation drivers sit relative to rivals?
Which resources and capabilities pass VRIO and can therefore yield sustained advantage?
How do internal and external findings combine into a decision-relevant situation assessment with prioritized issues?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SWOT_SYNTHESIS pairs capabilities to opportunities with priorities

competency_questions.question: Does the firm have a competitive advantage, expressed as a relative-cost or willingness-to-pay gap, and from which activities?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITIVE_ADVANTAGE_DIAGNOSIS states advantage as a measurable gap

competency_questions.question: How durable is the advantage: what moat protects it, what erodes it, and is it vulnerable to disruption?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOAT_DURABILITY_ASSESS and DISRUPTION_RESPONSE rate durability and threats

competency_questions.question: Which generic strategy and distinctive position, with what tradeoffs and activity fit, should the firm choose?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GENERIC_STRATEGY_CHOICE and POSITIONING_TRADEOFFS yield one coherent position

competency_questions.question: What business model (value proposition, revenue model, cost structure) captures value from the chosen position?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUSINESS_MODEL_DESIGN yields a coherent revenue-and-cost logic

competency_questions.question: Is there a value-innovation or blue-ocean move that breaks the cost-differentiation tradeoff and is still defensible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BLUE_OCEAN_VALUE_INNOVATION yields a tested ERRC hypothesis

competency_questions.question: Which strategic moves (market entry, diversification, M&A/alliance) create value, and is the chosen strategy robust and validated before commitment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: entry/diversification/M&A nodes pass value-creation tests and STRATEGY_VALIDATION_GOVERNANCE gates the decision

glossary.definition: the precise strategic question being decided: the move, unit of analysis, horizon, and criteria
Porter's model of industry structure: rivalry, entrants, substitutes, buyer power, supplier power
ability to earn above-average returns via lower relative cost or a willingness-to-pay premium
a structural barrier that sustains advantage against imitation (scale, network effects, switching costs, intangibles, cost edge)
a coherent competitive logic: cost leadership, differentiation, or focus
a distinctive set of activities and deliberate tradeoffs that make the firm different and hard to imitate
a test of whether a resource is valuable, rare, inimitable, and organized to exploit
raising buyer value and lowering cost simultaneously by changing the factors competed on (blue ocean)
a good-enough, often lower-end innovation that improves until it displaces incumbents (Christensen)
how a firm creates, delivers, and captures value: value proposition, revenue model, cost structure

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established competitive-strategy literature (Porter 1980 Competitive Strategy; Porter 1985 Competitive Advantage; Magretta 2012 Understanding Michael Porter; Christensen 1997 The Innovator's Dilemma; Barney VRIO; Kim & Mauborgne Blue Ocean Strategy) and standard strategy practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Frame the strategic decision as a well-posed question with objective, unit of analysis (firm/business-unit/market), time horizon, and decision criteria before any analysis.
contradictors: analyst who runs frameworks before fixing the question

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: a well-posed question prevents framework-for-its-own-sake analysis
pros.example: ask 'should we enter segment X by 2027' not 'analyze the industry'

cons.claim: an ill-framed question makes every downstream framework answer the wrong thing
cons.example: running five-forces with no decision to inform yields an unused deck

acceptance_tests: question stated as a decision on a named unit and horizon
decision criteria explicit

nodes.definition: Define the relevant industry/market boundaries: products, geographies, buyer groups, and substitutes that bound where rivalry and the analysis apply.
contradictors: analyst who defines the market too narrowly to fit a conclusion

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: a correct market boundary sets which forces and rivals are even relevant
pros.example: include ride-hail and transit as substitutes when scoping car rental

cons.claim: a mis-drawn boundary inflates or hides rivalry and substitutes
cons.example: defining 'our market' as only premium players understates substitution

acceptance_tests: boundary justified by buyer switching and substitution
substitutes explicitly listed

nodes.definition: Scan the macro-environment (political, economic, social, technological, environmental, legal) for forces that shift industry attractiveness or strategic options.
contradictors: analyst who treats macro trends as deterministic

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: macro scanning surfaces option-changing shifts before rivals react
pros.example: spot battery-cost decline reshaping auto economics early

cons.claim: undisciplined PESTEL produces a long ungrounded trend list
cons.example: listing 50 trends with no link to the decision adds noise

nodes.definition: Assess industry structure via Porter's five forces (rivalry, new entrants, substitutes, buyer power, supplier power) to estimate average profit potential.
contradictors: analyst who uses five forces as a checklist without structural reasoning

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: five forces explains why average profitability differs across industries
pros.example: airlines vs software margins follow from structure, not effort

cons.claim: applied as a static checklist it misses dynamics and complementors
cons.example: scoring forces once ignores how platforms reshape buyer power

failure_modes: confusing industry attractiveness with firm position
acceptance_tests: each force rated with named structural drivers
attractiveness tied to decision, not absolute

nodes.definition: Profile rivals and map strategic groups: their positioning, cost structure, capabilities, likely moves, and mobility barriers between groups.
contradictors: analyst who lists competitors without modeling their likely response

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: strategic-group maps reveal where rivalry concentrates and where white space sits
pros.example: map low-cost vs premium clusters to find an underserved mid-tier

cons.claim: ignoring competitor reaction makes a 'good' move unprofitable after retaliation
cons.example: a price cut copied instantly erodes everyone's margin

nodes.definition: Segment buyers and define their jobs-to-be-done, willingness to pay, and unmet needs to ground positioning and value-proposition choices in real demand.
contradictors: analyst who segments by demographics instead of needs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: need-based segmentation reveals where differentiation can command price
pros.example: find a job mainstream rivals underserve and price to it

cons.claim: demographic-only segmentation misallocates the value proposition
cons.example: targeting 'millennials' instead of the job they hire the product for

nodes.definition: Decompose the firm's value chain into primary and support activities to locate cost drivers and differentiation sources relative to rivals.
contradictors: analyst who maps activities but never compares them to rivals

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: locating cost and differentiation drivers by activity makes advantage concrete
pros.example: trace low cost to a specific procurement and logistics linkage

cons.claim: a value-chain map without rival comparison cannot show advantage
cons.example: listing activities proves nothing about relative position

nodes.definition: Audit resources and capabilities and test each for value, rarity, inimitability, and organization (VRIO) to identify what can yield sustained advantage.
contradictors: analyst who calls every asset a 'core competence'

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: VRIO separates parity resources from genuine advantage sources
pros.example: only the inimitable, organized capability survives the test

cons.claim: labeling parity resources as advantages overstates defensibility
cons.example: calling a common ERP system a 'core competence' misleads strategy

nodes.definition: Integrate external (opportunities, threats) and internal (strengths, weaknesses) findings into a decision-relevant SWOT that pairs capabilities to opportunities.
contradictors: analyst who produces an unprioritized four-box list

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: SWOT done well forces internal and external findings into matched actions
pros.example: pair an inimitable capability to an underserved segment as the move

cons.claim: a generic four-box SWOT lists items without action or priority
cons.example: an unranked grid that no decision can use

nodes.definition: Diagnose whether and why the firm can earn above-average returns: lower relative cost, willingness-to-pay premium, or both, and the activities that produce it.
contradictors: analyst who asserts advantage without a cost or WTP basis

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: grounding advantage in relative cost or WTP makes strategy testable
pros.example: quantify a cost gap or a price premium tied to specific activities

cons.claim: asserted advantage with no cost/WTP basis is wishful positioning
cons.example: claiming 'better brand' without a measurable WTP premium

failure_modes: cost and differentiation pursued without fit
acceptance_tests: advantage expressed as a relative-cost or WTP gap with named drivers
sustainability tested against imitation

nodes.definition: Assess the durability of advantage: identify moats (scale economies, network effects, switching costs, intangible assets, cost edge) and threats that erode them.
contradictors: analyst who confuses current high margins with a durable moat

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: naming the moat type tells you what reinvestment protects it
pros.example: a network-effect moat needs liquidity, not just brand spend

cons.claim: mistaking transient margins for a moat invites disruption
cons.example: high margins with no barrier attract entrants who compete them away

acceptance_tests: moat tied to a concrete imitation barrier
erosion threats and reinvestment named

nodes.definition: Choose a coherent generic strategy (cost leadership, differentiation, or focus) and avoid being stuck-in-the-middle by aligning activities to the chosen logic.
contradictors: analyst who pursues cost and differentiation at once without a basis

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: a single coherent generic strategy aligns activities and avoids contradiction
pros.example: focus differentiation concentrates spend where WTP is highest

cons.claim: chasing cost and differentiation without integration leaves the firm stuck in the middle
cons.example: cutting cost while adding features dilutes both positions

acceptance_tests: one dominant strategy chosen with activities aligned
no contradictory cost/differentiation spend

nodes.definition: Define a distinctive position via deliberate tradeoffs and activity fit so that being different is hard to imitate (Porter/Magretta), not just operationally effective.
contradictors: analyst who equates operational effectiveness with strategy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: tradeoffs and fit make a position defensible because imitation forces straddling costs
pros.example: choosing not to serve a segment is what protects the position

cons.claim: copying best practices is operational effectiveness, not strategy, and converges margins
cons.example: everyone adopting the same tools competes profits away

acceptance_tests: position rests on explicit tradeoffs and reinforcing activity fit
what-not-to-do list present

nodes.definition: Design the business model: value proposition, customer segments, revenue model, cost structure, key activities/resources, and how they reinforce the strategy.
contradictors: analyst who designs a value prop with no value-capture logic

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: an explicit revenue and cost model makes value capture, not just value creation, testable
pros.example: pair a freemium funnel to a clear monetization and cost-to-serve

cons.claim: a value proposition with no capture logic creates value rivals or customers keep
cons.example: great product, no pricing power, zero economic profit

failure_modes: cost structure mismatched to revenue model

nodes.definition: Explore value-innovation moves that break the cost-differentiation tradeoff by eliminating, reducing, raising, and creating factors to open uncontested space.
contradictors: analyst who treats blue-ocean claims as exempt from value-capture discipline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: value innovation can lift WTP and cut cost together by changing the factor set
pros.example: drop costly factors customers do not value and add cheap ones they do

cons.claim: blue-ocean narratives often skip whether the new space is defensible or profitable
cons.example: an 'uncontested' market that is uncontested because it is unprofitable

nodes.definition: Decide whether, when, and how to enter a market: entry mode (organic, alliance, acquisition), timing (pioneer vs follower), and required commitments versus reversibility.
contradictors: analyst who recommends entry without modeling incumbent response

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: matching entry mode and timing to advantage and incumbent reaction reduces costly entry failure
pros.example: enter via alliance when the capability gap is too large to build

cons.claim: committed entry without an advantage or exit option is hard to reverse
cons.example: sunk-cost entry into a fortified incumbent's core market

failure_modes: irreversible commitment with no exit option
acceptance_tests: entry justified by a transferable advantage and survivable incumbent response
exit/option value considered

nodes.definition: Decide corporate scope: which businesses to be in, testing diversification against the better-off, ownership, and attractiveness tests for value creation.
contradictors: analyst who diversifies for growth without a value-creation test

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: the attractiveness/better-off/ownership tests filter value-destroying diversification
pros.example: require a synergy a parent uniquely captures, not generic growth

cons.claim: diversification for growth alone destroys value via conglomerate discount
cons.example: entering an attractive but unrelated business with no shared advantage

acceptance_tests: each move passes attractiveness, better-off, and ownership tests
synergy is parent-specific

nodes.definition: Decide between build, ally, or acquire to close a capability or position gap, including target logic, integration risk, and alternatives to a deal.
contradictors: analyst who treats acquisition as the default growth lever

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: comparing build vs ally vs acquire prevents defaulting to the most irreversible option
pros.example: an alliance can secure a capability without integration risk

cons.claim: acquisitions overpay and fail integration when synergy is assumed not tested
cons.example: paying a premium for synergies that integration cannot realize

acceptance_tests: build/ally/acquire compared on synergy net of integration risk
walk-away alternative defined

nodes.definition: Assess disruptive-innovation threats and design a response: detect low-end/new-market disruption early and decide whether to defend, cannibalize, or build a separate unit.
contradictors: analyst who dismisses low-end entrants as low-margin and irrelevant

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: early classification of disruptive vs sustaining threats prevents being out-competed from below
pros.example: spot a good-enough low-end entrant before it moves upmarket

cons.claim: ignoring low-margin entrants is exactly how incumbents get disrupted
cons.example: rational margin focus blinds the leader to a rising substitute

acceptance_tests: threat classified as sustaining or disruptive with evidence
response weighs cannibalization vs disruption

nodes.definition: Stress-test the chosen strategy against alternative futures and competitor responses to find where it breaks and which bets are robust versus fragile.
contradictors: analyst who tests only the base case

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: testing the strategy across scenarios reveals fragile bets before commitment
pros.example: find that the plan only works if input costs stay low

cons.claim: a single base-case plan hides downside and competitor-reaction risk
cons.example: a strategy validated only under the rosy forecast

acceptance_tests: strategy payoff evaluated under at least one adverse scenario and a competitor-response scenario
fragile bets flagged with course-change triggers

nodes.definition: Validate the recommended strategy against internal consistency, evidence, and feasibility, and govern the go/no-go decision with explicit criteria and review.
contradictors: analyst who finalizes a recommendation without a falsification test

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-priority upstream analysis or a key assumption for this node changes

pros.claim: an explicit consistency and evidence test catches incoherent or unsupported strategy before commit
pros.example: reject a plan whose cost and differentiation goals contradict

cons.claim: governance with no falsification test rubber-stamps a persuasive but wrong recommendation
cons.example: approving a deck because it is confident, not because it is sound

acceptance_tests: strategy passes internal-consistency, evidence, and feasibility tests
go/no-go recorded with criteria

edges.why_related: the framed question fixes which industry and unit the boundary must cover
edges.risk_of_conflict: scoping before framing analyzes the wrong market
edges.example: scope car-sharing only after the entry question is set
edges.resolution_rule: fix the question before drawing the market boundary

edges.why_related: force analysis applies only within a defined industry boundary
edges.benefit_of_coupling: forces scored on the right scope
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong boundary mis-scores rivalry and substitutes
edges.example: include transit as a substitute once the market is defined
edges.resolution_rule: settle the boundary before scoring forces

edges.why_related: macro scanning targets the trends relevant to the defined market
edges.risk_of_conflict: unscoped PESTEL drifts off the decision
edges.example: scan auto-relevant tech trends after scoping
edges.resolution_rule: scope the market before listing macro trends

edges.why_related: the competitor set is defined by the market boundary
edges.risk_of_conflict: boundary errors add or omit rivals
edges.example: include adjacent-market rivals after scoping
edges.resolution_rule: define the boundary before profiling rivals

edges.why_related: buyer groups in scope determine which segments to analyze
edges.risk_of_conflict: out-of-scope segments waste analysis
edges.example: segment in-scope buyers after scoping
edges.resolution_rule: scope buyer groups before segmenting

edges.why_related: activities expose the resources and capabilities to test with VRIO
edges.risk_of_conflict: auditing capabilities without activities floats abstractly
edges.example: test the procurement capability VRIO finds in the chain
edges.resolution_rule: map the chain before the VRIO audit

edges.why_related: force findings supply the opportunities and threats in SWOT
edges.risk_of_conflict: SWOT without structure lists ungrounded threats
edges.example: derive entry-barrier threat from the forces
edges.resolution_rule: complete five forces before SWOT

edges.why_related: VRIO results supply the strengths and weaknesses in SWOT
edges.risk_of_conflict: SWOT strengths without VRIO overstate advantage
edges.example: list only VRIO-passing capabilities as strengths
edges.resolution_rule: complete the audit before SWOT

edges.why_related: competitor positions define relative strengths and threats in SWOT
edges.risk_of_conflict: absolute SWOT ignores rivals
edges.example: frame a strength relative to the closest rival
edges.resolution_rule: profile rivals before SWOT

edges.why_related: activity cost drivers are the basis for a relative-cost advantage claim
edges.risk_of_conflict: advantage without activity basis is asserted
edges.example: trace a cost gap to a specific activity linkage
edges.resolution_rule: map the chain before diagnosing advantage

edges.why_related: VRIO-passing capabilities are the source of sustained advantage
edges.risk_of_conflict: advantage from parity resources is illusory
edges.example: attribute advantage to the inimitable capability
edges.resolution_rule: finish the audit before diagnosing advantage

edges.why_related: segment WTP is the basis for a differentiation/premium advantage claim
edges.risk_of_conflict: differentiation without WTP is unpriced
edges.example: tie a price premium to a measured segment need
edges.resolution_rule: measure WTP before claiming differentiation

edges.why_related: you can only assess durability of an advantage that has been diagnosed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: durability grounded in a real edge
edges.risk_of_conflict: rating a moat with no advantage is empty
edges.example: assess durability of the diagnosed cost edge
edges.resolution_rule: diagnose advantage before rating its moat

edges.why_related: the diagnosed advantage type determines the coherent generic strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing a strategy against the advantage type fails
edges.example: pick cost leadership only if the cost edge is real
edges.resolution_rule: diagnose advantage before choosing generic strategy

edges.why_related: the generic strategy bounds which tradeoffs and position are coherent
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning that fights the generic strategy straddles
edges.example: focus-differentiate then choose what not to serve
edges.resolution_rule: choose the generic strategy before positioning

edges.why_related: segment needs define the distinctive value proposition to position around
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning without needs is arbitrary
edges.example: position around the highest-WTP unmet job
edges.resolution_rule: map needs before positioning

edges.why_related: the position and its tradeoffs constrain the value-capture and cost model
edges.risk_of_conflict: a model that contradicts the position breaks fit
edges.example: build revenue logic around the chosen tradeoffs
edges.resolution_rule: fix positioning before designing the model

edges.why_related: noncustomer and unmet-need analysis seeds value-innovation factor changes
edges.risk_of_conflict: value innovation without demand is novelty for its own sake
edges.example: raise factors noncustomers actually value
edges.resolution_rule: study needs before redesigning the value curve

edges.why_related: industry attractiveness conditions whether entry can earn returns
edges.risk_of_conflict: entering an unattractive structure burns capital
edges.example: weigh entry against high entry barriers
edges.resolution_rule: assess structure before deciding entry

edges.why_related: a transferable advantage is the precondition for profitable entry
edges.risk_of_conflict: entry without an edge fails against incumbents
edges.example: enter only where the cost edge transfers
edges.resolution_rule: diagnose advantage before entry

edges.why_related: predicted incumbent response shapes the entry mode and timing
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring retaliation makes entry unprofitable
edges.example: time entry to avoid an incumbent price war
edges.resolution_rule: model rival response before entry

edges.why_related: shared capabilities are the better-off basis for diversification
edges.risk_of_conflict: diversifying with no shared capability destroys value
edges.example: extend a unique capability into a related business
edges.resolution_rule: audit capabilities before diversifying

edges.why_related: the advantage must be transferable for diversification to be better-off
edges.risk_of_conflict: untransferable advantage yields conglomerate discount
edges.example: diversify only where the edge travels
edges.resolution_rule: diagnose advantage before scoping

edges.why_related: the chosen corporate scope defines what to build, ally, or acquire
edges.risk_of_conflict: deals without a scope thesis chase the wrong targets
edges.example: acquire only to fill the scoped capability gap
edges.resolution_rule: set scope before choosing the deal

edges.why_related: the capability gap determines build vs ally vs acquire
edges.risk_of_conflict: deals that duplicate existing capability waste capital
edges.example: ally for a capability too costly to build
edges.resolution_rule: size the gap before choosing the deal mode

edges.why_related: entrant signals from profiling feed disruption-threat detection
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing low-end entrants delays the response
edges.example: flag a good-enough entrant from the rival scan
edges.resolution_rule: profile entrants before assessing disruption

edges.why_related: customer good-enough trajectories indicate disruptive vulnerability
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring overserved customers hides disruption
edges.example: track when good-enough meets the mainstream job
edges.resolution_rule: read demand trajectory before classifying disruption

edges.why_related: the chosen strategy is the object that scenarios stress-test
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing nothing leaves fragility hidden
edges.example: stress the cost strategy against input-cost spikes
edges.resolution_rule: choose the strategy before stress-testing it

edges.why_related: the business model's unit economics are stress-tested across scenarios
edges.risk_of_conflict: untested economics hide downside
edges.example: stress the model when CAC doubles
edges.resolution_rule: design the model before stress-testing it

edges.why_related: robustness results feed the final validation and go/no-go
edges.risk_of_conflict: governing without stress results approves fragile strategy
edges.example: require a passing robustness map before go
edges.resolution_rule: stress-test before the governance gate

edges.why_related: the chosen strategy is validated for internal consistency at the gate
edges.risk_of_conflict: an inconsistent strategy passes if ungated
edges.example: reject contradictory cost/differentiation goals
edges.resolution_rule: validate the strategy at the governance gate

edges.why_related: positioning fit is checked for coherence before commitment
edges.risk_of_conflict: incoherent positioning commits a straddle
edges.example: verify activity fit before go
edges.resolution_rule: check positioning fit at the gate

edges.why_related: model feasibility and value capture are validated before commitment
edges.risk_of_conflict: an uncaptured-value model is approved if ungated
edges.example: require positive validated unit economics
edges.resolution_rule: validate the model at the gate

edges.why_related: committing to one generic strategy tensions with breaking the cost-differentiation tradeoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: pursuing both straddles and value-innovates incoherently
edges.example: cost-focus vs a value-innovation that raises costly factors
edges.resolution_rule: prefer the generic strategy unless value innovation is validated as defensible and capturable

edges.why_related: a diagnosed sustainable advantage tensions with abandoning it for uncontested space
edges.risk_of_conflict: chasing blue ocean can discard a real moat
edges.example: leave a defended position for an unproven new space
edges.resolution_rule: keep the diagnosed advantage unless the new space is shown to be more defensible

edges.why_related: aggressive entry speed tensions with preserving durable defensibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: fast entry can sacrifice the moat that makes it pay
edges.example: rush entry before the moat is built
edges.resolution_rule: preserve the moat-building sequence unless a time-limited window dominates, with a decision record

edges.why_related: growth via diversification tensions with focusing the core advantage
edges.risk_of_conflict: diversifying dilutes the focused advantage
edges.example: spread into unrelated growth and weaken the core edge
edges.resolution_rule: focus the core advantage unless the diversification passes the better-off test

edges.why_related: acquiring capability tensions with building it internally from audited resources
edges.risk_of_conflict: buying duplicates capability you could build cheaper
edges.example: acquire a capability the audit shows is buildable
edges.resolution_rule: prefer building when the audit shows a feasible path unless time or scarcity dominates

edges.why_related: validation failure can trigger revisiting the original question and scope
edges.benefit_of_coupling: closes the loop on framing errors
edges.risk_of_conflict: an endless reframing loop stalls the decision
edges.example: validation reveals the question was the wrong unit of analysis
edges.resolution_rule: revisit framing only if validation fails on a materiality>=0.10 issue; stop after re-validation passes or 3 cycles

edges.why_related: both synthesize internal/external findings into a position view but at different rigor
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them lets SWOT substitute for rigorous diagnosis
edges.example: SWOT strengths vs a measured cost/WTP edge
edges.resolution_rule: use SWOT to organize, advantage diagnosis to decide; do not merge

conflict_axes.trigger: pursuing low cost and a WTP premium with the same activity system
resolution_order: confirm the diagnosed advantage type
commit to the matching generic strategy
align activities and cut contradictory spend
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the diagnosed advantage (cost or WTP) dominates; the firm commits to one logic to avoid being stuck in the middle
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: plan funds both a cost program and a premium-feature program at scale
conflict_axes.example: cutting cost while adding premium features dilutes both positions

conflict_axes.trigger: abandoning a defended advantage to open uncontested space
resolution_order: assess defensibility of current advantage
test defensibility and value capture of the new space
choose the more defensible, capturable option
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: keep the diagnosed advantage unless the new space is shown to be more defensible and value-capturing
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the new space is uncontested because it is unprofitable
conflict_axes.example: leaving a moated core for an unproven new market

conflict_axes.trigger: an attractive market that does not fit capabilities, or a strong capability with no attractive market
resolution_order: check capability fit to the opportunity
check market attractiveness
require both fit and attractiveness for commitment
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: a move must satisfy both capability fit and market attractiveness; neither view alone licenses commitment
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a move is justified by attractiveness alone with no capability fit
conflict_axes.example: entering a high-growth market the firm has no right to win

conflict_axes.trigger: growth pressure pushing diversification away from the core advantage
resolution_order: apply attractiveness, better-off, ownership tests
require a parent-specific synergy
focus the core unless the tests pass
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: focus on the core advantage dominates unless diversification passes the value-creation tests
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: diversification justified by growth alone without a value-creation test
conflict_axes.example: entering an attractive but unrelated business with no shared advantage

conflict_axes.trigger: closing a capability gap by acquisition versus organic build
resolution_order: size the gap and build feasibility
compare synergy net of integration risk
prefer the lower-risk path that fits timing
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: build when the audit shows a feasible path, unless time-to-market or scarcity makes acquiring net-better after integration risk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: acquisition chosen as the default with untested synergy
conflict_axes.example: paying a premium for a capability the firm could build cheaper

conflict_axes.trigger: entering early for advantage versus waiting to reduce uncertainty and free-ride learning
resolution_order: assess first-mover advantage durability
assess imitation and learning risk
time entry to where advantage is defensible
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: enter early only when first-mover advantages are durable; otherwise a fast-follower captures value at lower risk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: pioneering with no defensible first-mover advantage
conflict_axes.example: being first into a market where followers copy the playbook cheaply

conflict_axes.trigger: a disruptive threat that requires cannibalizing the profitable core model
resolution_order: classify the threat as disruptive or sustaining
weigh cannibalization cost vs disruption loss
consider a separate unit to pursue the disruption
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if the threat is genuinely disruptive, pre-empting via cannibalization or a separate unit dominates defending the legacy model
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a low-end entrant is dismissed as immaterial on margin grounds
conflict_axes.example: protecting a high-margin product while a good-enough entrant moves upmarket

conflict_axes.trigger: stakeholders demand a recommendation before validation and stress-testing are complete
resolution_order: identify the irreversibility of the decision
require validation proportional to irreversibility
escalate if speed forces an unvalidated commit
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for irreversible or high-stakes moves, validation rigor dominates speed; reversible moves may proceed on lighter evidence
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an irreversible commitment is requested with no robustness test
conflict_axes.example: approving a major entry on a base-case deck with no scenario stress test

conflict_axes.trigger: running every framework exhaustively instead of answering the decision
resolution_order: tie each framework to the framed question
run only analyses that change the decision
synthesize to a recommendation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: decision-relevant insight dominates exhaustive framework completion; analyses that cannot change the decision are dropped
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: analysis volume grows while the decision stays unaddressed
conflict_axes.example: a 200-page industry study that never states what to do

edge_cases.trigger: the market boundary is drawn to make the conclusion look attractive
edge_cases.failure_mode: rivalry and substitution understated by a self-serving boundary
edge_cases.example: excluding ride-hail when scoping car rental to inflate share
edge_cases.detection_method: test the boundary against buyer switching and substitution data
resolution: re-run five forces on the corrected scope

edge_cases.trigger: an advantage is claimed with no relative-cost or WTP basis
edge_cases.failure_mode: wishful positioning treated as a real edge
edge_cases.example: claiming 'better brand' without a measured WTP premium
edge_cases.detection_method: require the advantage to be expressed as a measurable gap with named drivers
resolution: tie advantage to a VRIO-passing activity

edge_cases.trigger: the firm funds both cost and differentiation programs without integration
edge_cases.example: cutting cost while adding premium features
edge_cases.detection_method: check activity spend for contradiction with the chosen generic strategy

edge_cases.trigger: current high margins are read as a durable moat
edge_cases.failure_mode: transient profit mistaken for defensibility, inviting entry
edge_cases.example: high margins with no barrier attract entrants who compete them away
edge_cases.detection_method: require a named imitation barrier behind any moat claim
resolution: identify the actual barrier or none

edge_cases.trigger: a low-end good-enough entrant is dismissed as immaterial
edge_cases.failure_mode: incumbent disrupted from below after ignoring the entrant
edge_cases.example: rational margin focus blinds the leader to a rising substitute
edge_cases.detection_method: track entrant improvement trajectory against the mainstream job
resolution: classify threat as disruptive or sustaining

edge_cases.trigger: an entry move ignores predicted incumbent retaliation
edge_cases.failure_mode: entry becomes unprofitable after a price war
edge_cases.example: entering an incumbent's core with no response model
edge_cases.detection_method: require a competitor-response scenario before entry approval

edge_cases.trigger: deal synergies are assumed rather than tested net of integration risk
edge_cases.example: paying a premium for synergies integration cannot realize
edge_cases.detection_method: discount synergies by integration risk and compare to build/ally

edge_cases.trigger: the strategy is validated only under the base-case forecast
edge_cases.failure_mode: fragile bets hidden until a downside scenario hits
edge_cases.example: a plan that only works if input costs stay low
edge_cases.detection_method: require at least one adverse and one competitor-response scenario

edge_cases.trigger: frameworks are run exhaustively without tying to the decision
edge_cases.example: a 200-page study that never states what to do
edge_cases.detection_method: require each analysis to map to the framed question and a possible decision change
resolution: drop analyses that cannot change the decision

edge_cases.trigger: a cost/differentiation tradeoff is modeled as a prerequisite rather than a conflict
edge_cases.failure_mode: dependency-conflict conflation hides a real tradeoff
edge_cases.example: treating value innovation as a step after generic strategy instead of a tradeoff
edge_cases.detection_method: check that tradeoffs are encoded as conflict edges/axes not dependencies
resolution: move the tradeoff to a conflict axis

edge_cases.trigger: a heuristic estimate is presented as observed or validated fact
edge_cases.failure_mode: heuristic overclaiming inflates confidence in the recommendation
edge_cases.example: reporting a heuristic market-share estimate as measured data
edge_cases.detection_method: check that all numeric values carry a heuristic label with no observed/validated claims

workflow.objective: fix the strategic question and the relevant market boundary
acceptance_tests: question stated as a decision on a named unit and horizon
boundary justified by substitution
workflow.do_first_because: the question and scope are the highest-coupling foundation every later analysis inherits

workflow.objective: assess industry structure, macro forces, rivals, and customer needs
acceptance_tests: each force rated with named drivers
segments defined by jobs and WTP
workflow.do_first_because: external structure conditions which positions can earn returns

workflow.objective: locate cost/differentiation drivers and VRIO-passing capabilities
acceptance_tests: activities benchmarked against rivals
capabilities VRIO-rated
workflow.do_first_because: internal cost/capability evidence is required before any advantage claim

workflow.objective: integrate external and internal findings into prioritized strategic issues
acceptance_tests: each SWOT item evidence-backed
SO/ST/WO/WT actions present
workflow.do_first_because: synthesis prevents downstream choices from cherry-picking findings

workflow.objective: diagnose advantage as a cost/WTP gap and assess its durability
acceptance_tests: advantage expressed as a relative-cost or WTP gap with drivers
moat tied to an imitation barrier
workflow.do_first_because: advantage diagnosis is the hinge every strategic choice depends on and is high-risk

workflow.objective: choose generic strategy, position with tradeoffs, and design the business model
acceptance_tests: one generic strategy chosen with aligned activities
position rests on explicit tradeoffs and fit
workflow.do_first_because: the core strategy must be coherent before exploring moves or innovations

workflow.objective: test whether a value-innovation move beats the chosen position
acceptance_tests: ERRC grid grounded in noncustomer needs
new space tested for defensibility and capture
workflow.do_first_because: value innovation is an option weighed against, not before, the coherent base strategy

workflow.objective: decide entry, corporate scope, deals, and disruption response
acceptance_tests: each move passes its value-creation/transferability test
incumbent and integration risks modeled
workflow.do_first_because: moves are committed only after a coherent advantage-based strategy exists

workflow.objective: stress-test the strategy and moves across scenarios and competitor responses
acceptance_tests: payoff evaluated under an adverse and a competitor-response scenario
fragile bets flagged with triggers
workflow.do_first_because: fragility must be exposed before any irreversible commitment is governed

workflow.objective: validate consistency, evidence, and feasibility and govern the go/no-go
acceptance_tests: strategy passes consistency, evidence, and feasibility tests
go/no-go recorded with criteria
workflow.do_first_because: no irreversible strategy is committed before a falsification and governance gate

priority_rationale.notes: advantage is the hinge of strategy

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible move is requested before validation completes
dominance_rules.rule: irreversible or high-risk decisions require validation proportional to irreversibility before commitment
dominance_rules.required_action: block the commitment until STRATEGY_VALIDATION_GOVERNANCE passes
dominance_rules.example: refuse to approve a major entry on a base-case deck

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is ready but its prerequisite is not finalized
dominance_rules.rule: do not finalize a node before its true prerequisites
dominance_rules.example: do not choose a generic strategy before advantage is diagnosed

dominance_rules.trigger: a confident number lacks a supporting source
dominance_rules.rule: evidence-label correctness dominates apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade unsupported numbers to heuristic and state limits
dominance_rules.example: label a market-share estimate heuristic unless measured

dominance_rules.trigger: a growth move conflicts with focusing the core advantage
dominance_rules.rule: focus the core advantage unless the move passes attractiveness, better-off, and ownership tests
dominance_rules.required_action: apply the value-creation tests before approving the move
dominance_rules.example: reject unrelated diversification justified by growth alone

dominance_rules.trigger: cost and differentiation programs are funded together without integration
dominance_rules.rule: commit to one generic strategy aligned with the diagnosed advantage
dominance_rules.example: stop adding premium features under a cost-leadership logic

dominance_rules.trigger: best-practice copying is presented as strategy
dominance_rules.rule: a defensible position requires deliberate tradeoffs and fit, not just operational effectiveness
dominance_rules.required_action: require explicit tradeoffs and a what-not-to-do list
dominance_rules.example: adopting the same tools as rivals is not a strategy

dominance_rules.trigger: a low-end entrant is dismissed on margin grounds
dominance_rules.rule: classify and respond to genuinely disruptive threats even when the entrant looks low-margin
dominance_rules.required_action: run the disruption classification and decide cannibalize/defend/separate-unit
dominance_rules.example: do not ignore a good-enough entrant moving upmarket

dominance_rules.trigger: a strategy is proposed for hard lock before tests pass
dominance_rules.rule: acceptance tests and review must pass before any hard lock
dominance_rules.required_action: hold the lock until validation_report shows pass
dominance_rules.example: do not finalize the recommendation before the consistency test

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk move would be auto-approved
dominance_rules.rule: human review is required for any node with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or irreversible commitment
dominance_rules.required_action: route to a human reviewer with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: escalate an M&A commitment for human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: analysis volume grows while the decision stays unaddressed
dominance_rules.rule: run only analyses that can change the decision
dominance_rules.required_action: drop analyses that cannot change the decision and synthesize
dominance_rules.example: cut an exhaustive study that never states what to do

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the strategic question and scope before running any framework
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a framework run against the wrong question or scope is rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: five-forces or SWOT started before the question is framed
anti_rework_rules.example: analyzing an industry with no decision to inform

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle the market boundary before scoring forces, rivals, or segments
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a wrong boundary forces re-scoring every external analysis
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: forces scored on an unjustified boundary
anti_rework_rules.example: excluding substitutes then re-running the analysis later

anti_rework_rules.rule: map the value chain and audit capabilities before diagnosing advantage
anti_rework_rules.rationale: advantage with no activity basis is asserted and gets reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: advantage claimed before the chain and VRIO are done
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming a cost edge with no activity-level cost gap

anti_rework_rules.rule: diagnose advantage before choosing a generic strategy or position
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a strategy chosen against the advantage type must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: generic strategy chosen before the cost/WTP basis exists
anti_rework_rules.example: picking cost leadership with no cost edge

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the position before designing the business model
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a model that contradicts the position is rework
anti_rework_rules.example: building pricing logic that fights the chosen position

anti_rework_rules.rule: commit to a coherent strategy before deciding entry, scope, or deals
anti_rework_rules.rationale: moves made without a strategy thesis chase wrong targets
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an acquisition pursued with no strategy thesis
anti_rework_rules.example: acquiring before knowing what advantage it serves

anti_rework_rules.rule: run consistency, evidence, and scenario tests before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before tests forces a costly reversal
anti_rework_rules.example: approving a strategy validated only under the base case

anti_rework_rules.rule: encode tradeoffs as conflict axes before writing dominance rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dominance rules without mapped conflicts resolve the wrong tension
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a dominance rule with no matching conflict axis
anti_rework_rules.example: a resolution rule for a tradeoff that is not modeled

anti_rework_rules.rule: obtain human review before any irreversible commitment
anti_rework_rules.rationale: irreversible moves cannot be undone if wrong

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete traceability from question to validation before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untraceable recommendations cannot be audited or repaired
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a decision with no link back to evidence
anti_rework_rules.example: a go decision with no recorded criteria
